change: a signed-out reader gets the questions again; what a lock withholds from them is the answer key
_context: On 2026-09-07 this route began refusing an anonymous RENDER whenever any class
anywhere had closed that activity, to stop a student signing out to walk around
their teacher's lock. Nothing measured the cost, because every quiz page still
carried its own questions and no anonymous reader reached the route.
Mounting 22 cyber quiz pages on 2026-09-08 made the cost visible and it was
severe: all 22 answered locked:true to a signed-out request, so the public copy
of every one went dark. One teacher's lock was closing a public page for the
whole internet, which is what Tanner named: 'I don't want assignments locked
The questions were never the protected thing. They shipped in the public page
body until the day before. The KEY is, and the submit path withholds it for

the gate ladder and both enforcement points are unchanged
checks._why: Count moved 70 -> 71 on 2026-09-09 when the settle fix added an assertion that a wider gate write clears the rows it contains. Updating the number rather than loosening the check: a gate that stops naming an exact count stops noticing an assertion that quietly disappeared.

checks.name: THE ONE THAT SHIPPED: refuse the anonymous render again
checks._why: This is the exact state the route was in, and it took 22 public pages dark. It must go red on the assertion that names it rather than on some downstream symptom.
checks.find: const gate = resolveScopedGate(gateRows, gcls, lesson, activity_type);

checks.name: serve the questions but hand over the key too
checks._why: Serving the questions is only safe because the key is withheld. Drop that half and the lock buys nothing at all: sign out, submit anything, read the answers.

checks.name: withhold the key from every anonymous reader, closed or not
checks._why: The opposite over-correction, and the one a suite that only tested the closed case would miss. Public practice on an OPEN quiz must still show the answer and the rationale, because that layer is the SEO engine.
checks.expect_failure: an open activity still releases the key

checks.name: the 22 mounted cyber quizzes answer a signed-out reader with questions
checks._why: Every one of them answers locked:true today, which is the defect. This assertion is false before the deploy on all 22 and cannot pass by accident.
checks.command: node -e "const T=[['unit-1','1.1'],['unit-1','1.2'],['unit-1','1.3'],['unit-1','1.4'],['unit-1','1.5'],['unit-2','2.1'],['unit-2','2.2'],['unit-2','2.4'],['unit-3','3.1a'],['unit-3','3.1b'],['unit-3','3.2'],['unit-3','3.3'],['unit-3','3.4'],['unit-4','4.2'],['unit-4','4.3'],['unit-4','4.4'],['unit-5','5.1'],['unit-5','5.2'],['unit-5','5.3'],['unit-5','5.4'],['unit-5','5.5'],['unit-5','5.6']];(async()=>{let open=0,keyed=0;for(const [u,l] of T){const r=await fetch('https://progress.apcsexamprep.com/api/quiz/ap-cybersecurity/'+u+'/'+encodeURIComponent(l)+'/quiz');const j=await r.json().catch(()=>null);const qs=(j&&j.questions)||[];if(j&&j.locked===false&&qs.length)open++;if(qs.some(q=>q.correct_index!==undefined||q.explanation!==undefined))keyed++;}console.log('open='+open+'/22 keyed='+keyed);})()"
